A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Avatar Forcing work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across appendix reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original avatar-generation results, controlled ablations and a human preference study with 22 participants.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results, reports a 42-participant preference study, and adds block-size and long-horizon experiments.

M1.justification: The architecture, training objectives, preference-pair construction and main Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix D.1 and Algorithm 2 present guidance, offset handling and caching as additional inference details; they do not establish a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: v2 explicitly adds evaluation beyond the training horizon through the motion-drift comparison in Figure 11. RealTalk, ViCo and HDTF, and the interactive, talking and listening tasks, otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix D.4 and Figure 11 add a standard autoregressive-diffusion comparator conditioned on clean motion context. The comparator sets in the existing interactive, talking and listening benchmarks are unchanged.

E3.justification: The human study expands from 22 participants evaluating 8 video sets to 42 evaluating 12. New ablations compare 2, 5 and 10 blocks with 50 training frames, and train an autoregressive comparator using 40 clean context frames plus 10 noisy frames. Existing benchmark protocols otherwise remain stable.

E4.justification: v2 adds two targeted analyses: diffusion forcing versus autoregressive diffusion for long-horizon motion drift, and block-count sensitivity for latency and generation quality. Existing user-motion, DPO and attention-mask ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests for these results. The increased human-study sample size changes evaluation scale, not uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces preference percentages after expanding the study: reactiveness changes from 66.4% to 73.0%, and overall preference from 80.1% to 80.3%. These are not same-setting performance gains. Figure 11 and Table 7 add drift and block-size results; Tables 1 and 3–6 retain their values. Table 7's lip-sync values have an unresolved metric inconsistency.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the independently guided vector field and cross-block offset in Equations 14–15. Existing diffusion-forcing, DPO, flow-matching and metric equations retain their substance; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The main contributions and claims remain causal real-time avatar generation, expressive interaction through synthetic preference pairs, approximately 500 ms latency, 6.8-fold speedup and over 80% overall human preference. The expanded evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the added experiments as supporting diffusion forcing's resistance to motion drift and a latency–quality tradeoff with block count. Appendix E newly acknowledges that diffusion forcing does not fully resolve exposure bias. Existing bodily-motion and controllability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 and Algorithm 2 substantially expand the inference specification: separate guidance branches, 10% condition dropout, offset flow times, separate KV caches and a stated cache capacity of 38. Conversely, v2 removes the guidance scale of 2 and code/weight release commitments; numerical values for the two guidance weights are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds InstructPix2Pix by Brooks et al. as a citation for independent classifier-free guidance. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against talking, listening and dyadic avatar methods are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an acknowledgment section and an inference-details subsection, moves supplementary ablations ahead of evaluation metrics, and makes limited wording and cross-reference edits. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds detailed Algorithm 2, the long-horizon comparison in Figure 11, and the block-size ablation in Table 7. Existing appendix Figures 11–14 are retained as Figures 12–15, with localized layout and spacing changes.

improvement.justification: The larger human study, targeted ablations, fuller inference specification and explicit exposure-bias limitation modestly strengthen support and transparency. These gains are tempered by missing guidance-weight values and a new inconsistency: Table 7 labels the default 6.723 as LSE-D, whereas retained Tables 1 and 6 report LSE-D 8.060 and LSE-C 6.723. The central benchmark results and claims remain unchanged.
